subject: Week 34: book the 9-month visit — iron rescreen and ASQ-3 ahead
bodyText:
This week
This is the CDC 9-month checklist in live action: getting to sitting on his own, transferring objects hand to hand, raking food, varied babble strings, and reacting when you leave the room. The well-visit window opens Day 252 (Jan 18) — the pediatrician will run a hemoglobin rescreen and often a standardized ASQ-3 developmental screen, so book now and start a notes file: babble variety, feeding, sleep, anything that nags at you.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Shyness or fear around strangers and lifting arms to be picked up — both are on-schedule 9-month social behavior.
- [monitor] No babble strings, no response to his name, or no object transfer between hands — none is an emergency, all belong in the visit notes.
- [call within 24h] New wheezing, or an illness that stops improving after day three.
- [call now] Fever ≥102°F (rectal) with lethargy, labored breathing, or blue lips — call now or 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Lock the paid swim slot before the conversion window closes Wednesday Jan 6: La Petite Baleen runs perpetual enrollment at $130-138/mo, or check JCCSF Water Babies for openings (waitlists cap at five). One program only — there is no dose-response evidence under 12 months. La Petite Baleen tuition: https://www.swimlpb.com/swim-classes/tuition
- Play object-permanence games daily: hide a toy under a cup, pause, reveal. Looking for hidden objects is the 9-month cognitive checkpoint, and predictable surprise is the engagement mechanism. CDC 9-month milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
- Read 30 min/day but slow down: pause after he vocalizes and respond as if it were a word — that serve-and-return loop is the active ingredient. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Rehearse short separations with a fixed ritual — same phrase, brief exit, prompt return. Separation protest is object permanence applied to people; predictable exits shrink it.

Upcoming
- Day 240 (Jan 6, 2027): paid-swim conversion window closes — last day to hold the queue position.
- Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — book this week to land early in the window; influenza #2 if this is his first flu season, iron rescreen, possible ASQ-3.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Uses fingers to 'rake' food toward herself
  AAP window: day 210-270
  What to look for: Pre-pincer grasp. Coincides with starting finger foods.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-fingers-rake/complete

- Crawls on hands and knees, or scoots
  AAP window: day 210-330
  What to look for: Some babies skip crawling and go straight to cruising — that is within normal range.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/crawls/complete

- Moves from sitting into a crawl or lie-down position
  AAP window: day 210-330
  What to look for: Postural transition. Predicts comfortable independent exploration.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/gets-from-sit-to-crawl/complete

- Cries or protests when a parent leaves the room
  AAP window: day 210-365
  What to look for: Peak separation anxiety. Healthy attachment, even when it makes drop-off hard.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/cries-when-parent-leaves/complete

- Catches himself with his arms when tipping over while sitting
  AAP window: day 210-300
  What to look for: Protective arm extension — reaching out to break a sideways or forward topple. Makes independent sitting safe enough for hands-busy play.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/catches-self-when-sitting/complete
